title: Number tonight's tenant exports so they stay numbered

blocks.text: The nightly export builds one task per tenant at 23:00 and hands the list to a scheduler, which runs the tasks whenever it has capacity: sometimes in order, sometimes last task first. Each export is stamped with its task number, and the morning report matches stamps against the plan. Last week the report showed tenants under the wrong numbers, and one tenant that was added to the admin screen at 23:05 got exported although it wasn't in the 23:00 plan.
`ExportPlan` already builds the list of tasks. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ExportPlan.java`:

items: `task(tenants, index)`: the task for the tenant at `index`, numbered `index + 1`.

blocks.text: When you're done, every task exports the tenant and the number it was planned with, whatever order the scheduler runs the tasks in and whatever the caller does to its list after `tasksFor` returns. About three lines in total.

cases.says: tasks run in the order they were built export each tenant with its number, from 1
building the tasks exports nothing; only running them does
a task's number is fixed when the task is built, so running the tasks in reverse order still exports each tenant with its own number
a task exports the tenant that was at its index when it was built, even after the caller reorders or edits its list

origin.section: A Lambda Copies the Locals It Uses, So They Must Be Effectively Final

concepts: A lambda copies the values of the locals it captures when it is created; for a reference that is the reference, so the object behind it can still change.
